title: Exact first-detection probability in a locally monitored solvable quantum circuit
authors: Cecilia De Fazio, Igor Lesanovsky, Gabriele Perfetto
abstract: We study the interplay between local stroboscopic measurements and the unitary quantum circuit dynamics of the deterministic Floquet-quantum East model. We derive exact analytical results for the probability of first detecting a subset of qubits back in their initial state. This is achieved via a renewal equation linking the first-detection probability to the subsystem Loschmidt echo, which encodes the effective open dynamics of the monitored qubits. The resulting statistics exhibit two regimes set by the competition between the measurement probing time and the relaxation timescale of the unitary circuit dynamics: while infrequent monitoring leads to geometric first-detection statistics, frequent monitoring induces correlations that manifest as deviations from this geometric behavior. These results provide a rare exact characterization of how local measurement backaction reshapes detection statistics in an interacting quantum many-body system. In our local protocol, return probabilities are controlled by the size of the monitored subregion and can therefore be accessed on digital quantum simulators via local mid-circuit measurements.
summary: This work provides exact analytical results for the probability of first detecting a specific state in a quantum circuit undergoing local monitoring. By relating this probability to the subsystem Loschmidt echo, the authors characterize how measurement frequency dictates the detection statistics. The findings reveal a transition from simple geometric decay to complex, correlated behavior as the measurement rate changes.
main_problem: The paper derives exact analytical results for the probability of first detecting a subset of qubits back in their initial state within a locally monitored quantum circuit.
main_result: The first-detection probability exhibits two distinct regimes: geometric statistics for infrequent monitoring, and correlated deviations from this behavior for frequent monitoring.
method: The analysis employs a renewal equation linking the first-detection probability to the subsystem Loschmidt echo, utilizing generating functions and pole analysis for asymptotic behavior.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the deterministic Floquet-quantum East model (DFQEM), an interacting quantum circuit subjected to local stroboscopic measurements.
key_observables: First-Detection Return Probability (FDRP), Subsystem Loschmidt Echo, Coefficient of Variation (CV).
important_parameters: Measurement probing time ($	au$), monitored subregion size ($\ell$), and the ratio between $	au$ and the relaxation timescale ($2\ell$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the initial state of the unmonitored qubits is a bi-translationally invariant product state and relies on the renewal equation framework.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the measurement protocol, the folded space representation for calculation, and the dependence of the Loschmidt echo and FDRP on measurement parameters.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the local monitoring protocol and the FDRP, deriving the renewal equation linking it to the Loschmidt echo, and then analyzing the resulting statistics in the limits of infrequent versus frequent measurements using generating functions.
why_interesting: It provides a rare exact characterization of how local measurement backaction fundamentally reshapes detection statistics in an interacting quantum many-body system, which is crucial for understanding open quantum dynamics.
